precepts.text: Agabus signified by the Spirit that there should be great dearth throughout all the world, which came to pass in the days of Claudius Caesar. He dreamed it under Caligula, and it took place years later under Claudius. We're telling y'all famine is coming; some of y'all are preparing, some are not.
precepts.point: Discussion of Idi Amin, Uganda, and South Africa: Idi Amin expelled the Asian and European merchants from Uganda and handed their businesses to Ugandans who had no experience in the imports and exports of that merchandise, and the stores collapsed. Today in South Africa the xenophobia is the same error: legal migrants from Ghana, Nigeria, and the ECOWAS region with legitimate small businesses are being beaten, driven from hospitals, and flown home, while about 90 percent of the businesses and the land are owned by white people. They turn against their own brothers while the real owners of the country are standing in front of them. Black people in America do the same thing when we riot and burn down stores in our own neighborhoods instead of saving our money and opening our own. Nobody has solutions to the problems, and the white man's solution is jail time.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.why:
“And the famine was sore in the land.” There have always been famines. The only difference now is that we think a famine could never happen, because we have grown accustomed to living here.

Luke records one: “there stood up one of them named Agabus, and signified by the spirit that there should be great dearth throughout all the world: which came to pass in the days of Claudius Cesar.” It did not come to pass the moment Agabus signified it. He had it under Caligula; Caligula was put to death, and Claudius came in, some five to ten years later, and then the dearth came.

That is said for a reason. We are telling our people famine is coming, and some are preparing while some are not. The word does not fail just because it does not happen the next day. In Genesis 43 the corn from Egypt was eaten up, and Jacob had to send his sons back, Benjamin with them, with Judah saying, “that we may live, and not die, both we, and thou, and also our little ones.” The famine came, as Joseph said it would.

note.label: Recovering the Remnant: Worldwide Blitz

precepts.why:
“Go not into the way of the Gentiles”: in this verse that includes the other eleven tribes. “And into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not”: that is the Northern Kingdom. Why? Because it was not their time yet. The Lord said he would raise the tents of Judah first. “But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel”: that starts with Judah first.

Some are confused and think this is new. It is not; it has always been taught. Acts shows the order being followed after Christ: “Now they which were scattered abroad upon the persecution that arose about Stephen travelled as far as Phenice, and Cyprus, and Antioch, preaching the word to none but unto the Jews only.”

To none but the Jews only: only to Judah. They were primarily dealing with Judah first.

That does not mean the rest were never to be reached. Christ himself went to Samaria in John 4 and taught the Samaritans for a few days, because he knew the time was coming to deal with them. Judah first, and then the other tribes.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
“Now they which were scattered abroad upon the persecution that arose about Stephen travelled as far as Phenice, and Cyprus, and Antioch, preaching the word to none but unto the Jews only.”

That is the unto you first in action. The scattered disciples preached to none but the Jews only, the southern kingdom, according to the order in which the tribes are redeemed.

precepts.text: The scattered disciples preached to none but the Jews only, yet spoke to the Grecians, showing the Grecians were those Jews.
precepts.point: Those who argue the Most High deals with the Greeks too are themselves so-called African American, West Indian, Haitian, and Jamaican, and they do not fit the title. To claim the grafting you must prove by your records which Gentile nation you are, and each Gentile nation had judgments that are not yet fulfilled.

note.label: Acts 6: The Grecians Were Greek-Speaking Israelites

precepts.why:
The scattered disciples went “preaching the word to none but unto the Jews only. And some of them were men of Cyprus and Cyrene, which, when they were come to Antioch, spake unto the Grecians, preaching the Lord Jesus.”

To none but the Jews only, and yet they spoke to the Grecians. So the Grecians were those Jews. People who do not know the history hear Grecians and assume the Most High began dealing with the heathen nations under Christ. But the Grecians are Israelites scattered into the Greek provinces during the Greek captivity, the same way our people dropped off in England, the Caribbean and the Americas take the name of the land that enslaved them and are called African American.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

precepts.why:
“Now they which were scattered abroad upon the persecution that arose about Stephen travelled as far as Phenice, and Cyprus, and Antioch, preaching the word to none but unto the Jews only.” The same scattering that sent Philip to Samaria sent others to Phenice, Cyprus and Antioch, and they preached to none but the Jews only.

The same holds for Philip in Samaria. He was preaching Christ to the Jews who lived in Samaria, not yet to the Gentiles. The Most High moves in order, causing interruptions and persecutions to push his chess pieces and further spread the gospel.

Send therefore to Joppa, and call hither Simon, whose surname is Peter.”

The Gentiles in Acts 11:1 are a reference to Cornelius. He was not Italian by nation. He was an Israelite who served as a general over a hundred men in the Roman army, just as today there are black generals and black soldiers in the American army, and America is an extension of ancient Rome.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
Cornelius was not the first of the northern kingdom to keep the law while scattered. Tobit was “of the tribe of Nephthali; Who in the time of Enemessar king of the Assyrians was led captive out of Thisbe.”

“I Tobit have walked all the days of my life in the ways of truth and justice, and I did many almsdeeds to my brethren, and my nation, who came with me to Nineve, into the land of the Assyrians.” When the tribe of Nephthali fell from the house of Jerusalem and “sacrificed unto the heifer Baal”, Tobit said, “But I alone went often to Jerusalem at the feasts, as it was ordained unto all the people of Israel by an everlasting decree.”

Tobit, of the northern kingdom, carried captive to Nineveh, still walked in truth and went up to Jerusalem. He was a remnant keeping the law, and Cornelius is the same: a man of the scattered north, giving alms and keeping the commandments.

precepts.text: Every man child was to be circumcised, and it was a token of the covenant between the Most High and Abraham's seed.
precepts.point: To understand circumcision and uncircumcision you have to go to the origin: circumcision was the token, the sign, the seal of the covenant the Most High made with Abraham, a visible confirmation carried through all the generations.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
When Peter came up to Jerusalem, “they that were of the circumcision contended with him, Saying, Thou wentest in to men uncircumcised, and didst eat with them.” The complaint was about Peter dealing with the Gentiles, meaning the northern kingdom. There had been contention between the northern and southern kingdom ever since the split under Solomon.

To understand circumcision and uncircumcision you have to go to the origin: “This is my covenant, which ye shall keep, between me and you and thy seed after thee; Every man child among you shall be circumcised. And ye shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin; and it shall be a token of the covenant betwixt me and you.”

Circumcision was the token, the sign, of the covenant the Most High made with Abraham, a visible confirmation carried through all the generations of his seed.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

Mattathias, son of John, son of Simeon: from him came the Hasmonean dynasty, meaning the house of Simeon. He and his house are the ones who went about restoring the law and circumcision.

precepts.text: The Assideans, mighty men devoted to the law, joined Mattathias and circumcised the uncircumcised valiantly. The Jewish Encyclopedia notes the Assideans, or Hasidim, were pious men devoted to the law from whom the Pharisees are held to have developed.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
“Then came there unto him a company of Assideans who were mighty men of Israel, even all such as were voluntarily devoted unto the law.”

“Then Mattathias and his friends went round about, and pulled down the altars: And what children soever they found within the coast of Israel uncircumcised, those they circumcised valiantly.” The Assideans, mighty men devoted to the law, joined Mattathias and circumcised the uncircumcised valiantly. The Jewish Encyclopedia notes that the Assideans, or Hasidim, were pious men devoted to the law, from whom the Pharisees are held to have developed.

So the circumcision was primarily the southern kingdom, Judah, raised in the law, and the Pharisees, who pushed circumcision above everything, even above faith and the commandments. The uncircumcision was the northern kingdom and the scattered Israelites. That is who contended with Peter.

precepts.text: What advantage hath the Jew, or profit of circumcision? Much every way, chiefly because to them were committed the oracles of God.
precepts.point: So the circumcision was primarily the southern kingdom, Judah, raised in the law, and the Pharisees who pushed circumcision above everything, even above faith and the commandments; the uncircumcision was the northern kingdom and the scattered Israelites.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
“What advantage then hath the Jew? or what profit is there of circumcision? Much every way: chiefly, because that unto them were committed the oracles of God.”

The circumcision, Judah, had the advantage of being raised in the law, because unto them were committed the oracles of God. That is why they held themselves apart from the uncircumcision and contended with Peter for eating with them.

precepts.text: Paul was circumcised the eighth day, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Pharisee, because the Pharisees upheld circumcision.
precepts.point: So the circumcision was primarily the southern kingdom, Judah, raised in the law, and the Pharisees who pushed circumcision above everything, even above faith and the commandments; the uncircumcision was the northern kingdom and the scattered Israelites.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
Paul was “Circumcised the eighth day, of the stock of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, an Hebrew of the Hebrews; as touching the law, a Pharisee.”

Paul was of the southern kingdom, Benjamin, and a Pharisee, and the Pharisees upheld circumcision. That is the party of the circumcision that contended with Peter.

precepts.text: Remember that ye being in time past Gentiles in the flesh, called uncircumcision by that which is called the circumcision.
precepts.point: Paul reminds the Israelites in Ephesus that in time past they were Gentiles in the flesh, called the uncircumcision, because under the Greeks it was unlawful to profess yourself a Jew, so Israel had to call themselves Greeks or Gentiles.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
“Wherefore remember, that ye being in time past Gentiles in the flesh, who are called Uncircumcision by that which is called the Circumcision in the flesh made by hands.”

Paul reminds the Israelites in Ephesus that in time past they were Gentiles in the flesh, called the uncircumcision by the circumcision. They were Israelites, but under the Greeks it was unlawful to profess yourself a Jew, so Israel had to call themselves Greeks or Gentiles.

precepts.text: It was not lawful to keep the Sabbath or the feasts or to profess to be a Jew, so Israel took on Gentile titles.
precepts.point: Paul reminds the Israelites in Ephesus that in time past they were Gentiles in the flesh, called the uncircumcision, because under the Greeks it was unlawful to profess yourself a Jew, so Israel had to call themselves Greeks or Gentiles.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
“Neither was it lawful for a man to keep sabbath days or ancient fasts, or to profess himself at all to be a Jew.”

It was not lawful to keep the Sabbath or the feasts or to profess to be a Jew. So Israel took on Gentile titles and called themselves Greeks or Gentiles. That is how Israelites came to be called the uncircumcision.

precepts.text: Whoever would not conform to the manners of the Gentiles was put to death, forcing Israel into Gentile customs.
precepts.point: Paul reminds the Israelites in Ephesus that in time past they were Gentiles in the flesh, called the uncircumcision, because under the Greeks it was unlawful to profess yourself a Jew, so Israel had to call themselves Greeks or Gentiles.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
“And whoso would not conform themselves to the manners of the Gentiles should be put to death. Then might a man have seen the present misery.”

Whoever would not conform to the manners of the Gentiles was put to death. That forced Israel into Gentile customs, and it is why the men Peter went in to could be Israelites and still be called uncircumcised and Gentiles.

precepts.text: Israel is swallowed up and shall be among the Gentiles as a vessel wherein is no pleasure.
precepts.point: Peter rehearses the vision from the beginning: he was in Joppa praying, and in a trance saw a vessel descend like a great sheet. That vessel is Israel, swallowed up and consumed among the Gentiles, made a vessel of no honour by learning their works and serving their idols.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
Peter rehearsed the matter from the beginning: “I was in the city of Joppa praying: and in a trance I saw a vision, A certain vessel descend, as it had been a great sheet.”

That vessel is Israel: “Israel is swallowed up: now shall they be among the Gentiles as a vessel wherein is no pleasure.” Israel was swallowed up and consumed among the Gentiles, made a vessel of no honour by learning their works and serving their idols.

precepts.text: The Most High cast down from heaven to the earth the beauty of Israel, cast down from rulership.
precepts.point: The sheet was let down from heaven by four corners, meaning Israel was cast down from a position of rulership to the earth into servitude, to be gathered again from the four corners as the outcasts of Israel.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
The sheet was “let down from heaven by four corners; and it came even to me.”

“How hath the Lord covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud in his anger, and cast down from heaven unto the earth the beauty of Israel.” Let down from heaven means Israel was cast down from a position of rulership to the earth, into servitude. The beauty of Israel was brought down, and that is what Peter saw let down before him.

precepts.text: The root of Jesse whom the Gentiles seek, and the Most High recovers the remnant and assembles the outcasts of Israel from the four corners of the earth.
precepts.point: The sheet was let down from heaven by four corners, meaning Israel was cast down from a position of rulership to the earth into servitude, to be gathered again from the four corners as the outcasts of Israel.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
The four corners of the sheet are the four corners Israel is gathered from. “And in that day there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the Gentiles seek.”

“The Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people”, “And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.”

Israel was cast down into servitude, to be gathered again from the four corners as the outcasts of Israel. The Gentiles who seek the root of Jesse are that remnant.

precepts.text: Men are shown themselves to be beasts, so the beasts in the vision are a representation of men.
precepts.point: Peter then saw four-footed beasts, wild beasts, creeping things, and fowls, which represent men, the unclean men of scattered Israel who took up idolatry.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
In the sheet Peter “saw fourfooted beasts of the earth, and wild beasts, and creeping things, and fowls of the air.”

“I said in mine heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts.” The beasts represent men: the unclean men of scattered Israel who took up idolatry.

precepts.text: It is unlawful for a Jew to keep company with one of another nation, but God showed Peter not to call any man common or unclean.
precepts.point: The voice said, "Arise, Peter; slay and eat," but Peter refused because nothing common or unclean had ever entered his mouth. The voice answered, "What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common," because it was never about food but about people.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
The voice said, “Arise, Peter; slay and eat.” Peter answered, “Not so, Lord: for nothing common or unclean hath at any time entered into my mouth.” The voice answered, “What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common”, because it was never about food but about people.

Peter said so himself in Cornelius' house: “Ye know how that it is an unlawful thing for a man that is a Jew to keep company, or come unto one of another nation; but God hath shewed me that I should not call any man common or unclean.” Any man, not any meat. And “one of another nation” points back to the split kingdom.

precepts.text: He will make them one nation under one king, no more two kingdoms, cleansed from their idols to be his people.
precepts.point: The "one of another nation" points back to the split kingdom, and the Most High promised to make the two nations one again under one king, cleansed from their idols.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
The Most High promised to make the two nations one again: “And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all: and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all.”

“Neither shall they defile themselves any more with their idols”, “but I will save them out of all their dwellingplaces, wherein they have sinned, and will cleanse them: so shall they be my people, and I will be their God.” That is what God hath cleansed: the northern kingdom, cleansed from their idols, made one nation with Judah under one king.

precepts.text: Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you, cleansing the scattered nation by the word.
precepts.point: To "slay and eat" means to teach and cleanse the scattered Israelites through the word of God.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
“Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you.”

To “slay and eat” means to teach and cleanse the scattered Israelites through the word of God. The word is what makes them clean. Peter was sent to Cornelius to speak the word, and by it the unclean men of the sheet were cleansed.

precepts.text: After two days he will revive us, and in the third day he will raise us up, a foreshadow of Israel restored.
precepts.point: The vision was done three times, symbolizing Israel being revived and raised up the third day.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
“And this was done three times.” The vision was done three times, symbolizing Israel being revived and raised up the third day.

“Come, and let us return unto the Lord: for he hath torn, and he will heal us; he hath smitten, and he will bind us up. After two days will he revive us: in the third day he will raise us up, and we shall live in his sight.” That is Israel restored, foreshadowed in the three times the sheet came down.

precepts.text: Destroy this temple and in three days I will raise it up, Christ's resurrection foreshadowing Israel's revival.
precepts.point: The vision was done three times, symbolizing Israel being revived and raised up the third day.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
“Jesus answered and said unto them, Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.”

Christ's resurrection on the third day foreshadows Israel's revival. As he was raised up in three days, Israel is raised up the third day, and that is what the vision done three times shows.

precepts.text: The disciples ask whether the Most High will at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel.
precepts.point: All was drawn up again into heaven, meaning Israel restored again to its position of rulership.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
“And all were drawn up again into heaven.” That means Israel restored again to its position of rulership. The sheet was let down from heaven when Israel was cast down into servitude, and drawn up again when Israel is raised up.

The disciples asked for exactly that: “Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel?”

precepts.text: A great voice from heaven says "Come up hither," and they ascend up to heaven in a cloud, Israel raised up again.
precepts.point: All was drawn up again into heaven, meaning Israel restored again to its position of rulership.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
“And they heard a great voice from heaven saying unto them, Come up hither. And they ascended up to heaven in a cloud; and their enemies beheld them.”

That is Israel raised up again. The sheet was drawn up again into heaven, and here they ascend up to heaven while their enemies behold them: Israel restored to its position of rulership.

precepts.text: The God of our fathers raised up Jesus and exalted him to be a Prince and a Saviour, to give repentance to Israel, so the repentance goes to Israel.
precepts.point: When they heard this they held their peace and glorified God, saying the Most High had also to the Gentiles granted repentance unto life. These Gentiles are the Israelites who took on Gentile customs, whether the northern kingdom broken off before Assyria when Pekah the son of Remaliah conspired against Judah, or Judah who became Gentiles under the Greeks.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
“When they heard these things, they held their peace, and glorified God, saying, Then hath God also to the Gentiles granted repentance unto life.”

Repentance goes to Israel: “The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom ye slew and hanged on a tree. Him hath God exalted with his right hand to be a Prince and a Saviour, for to give repentance to Israel, and forgiveness of sins.”

So the Gentiles granted repentance are Israelites who took on Gentile customs. Either the northern kingdom, broken off before Assyria when Pekah the son of Remaliah conspired against Judah, or Judah who became Gentiles under the Greeks. Christ was exalted to give repentance to Israel, and these Gentiles are Israel.

precepts.text: The Lord shall save the tents of Judah first, that the house of David not magnify itself against Judah.
precepts.point: The reason they preached to the Jews only is the prophecy that the Most High saves the tents of Judah first.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
“Now they which were scattered abroad upon the persecution that arose about Stephen travelled as far as Phenice, and Cyprus, and Antioch, preaching the word to none but unto the Jews only.” They went where the Israelites were scattered. Phenice was the coastal region north of Israel, modern Lebanon; Cyprus is an island in the eastern Mediterranean; Antioch was a major Roman city in ancient Syria, now Antakya, Turkey.

They preached to the Jews only because of the prophecy: “The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not magnify themselves against Judah.” The Most High saves the tents of Judah first.

Then some of them, “men of Cyprus and Cyrene”, came to Antioch and “spake unto the Grecians, preaching the Lord Jesus.” Those Grecians, or Hellenists, were Greek-speaking Jews. The Holman Christian Standard Bible calls them Hellenists, and the Zondervan compact Bible dictionary defines a Hellenist as a Jew who made Greek his tongue and adopted Greek ideas and practices.

precepts.text: Agrippa tells Paul, "Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian," meaning a follower of the anointed one.
precepts.point: The disciples were called Christians first in Antioch, and those disciples were Jews. Christians were not all nations or races as men think today; the Greek word Christianos comes from Christos, the anointed one, so a Christian is a kinsman of the Messiah and a follower of Christ, an anointed one.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
“And the disciples were called Christians first in Antioch.” Those disciples were Jews. Christians were not all nations or races as men think today. The Greek word Christianos comes from Christos, the anointed one, so a Christian is a kinsman of the Messiah and a follower of Christ, an anointed one.

“Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian.” Agrippa meant a follower of the anointed one. That is what the name meant when it was first given at Antioch.

precepts.text: If any man suffer as a Christian, let him not be ashamed, but glorify God on this behalf.
precepts.point: The disciples were called Christians first in Antioch, and those disciples were Jews. Christians were not all nations or races as men think today; the Greek word Christianos comes from Christos, the anointed one, so a Christian is a kinsman of the Messiah and a follower of Christ, an anointed one.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
“Yet if any man suffer as a Christian, let him not be ashamed; but let him glorify God on this behalf.”

Peter wrote this to Israel scattered abroad. A Christian is a follower of Christ, a kinsman of the Messiah, and to suffer as one is no shame but a reason to glorify God. That is the name the disciples, who were Jews, were first called in Antioch.

precepts.text: Saul sought letters to bind any of "this way," whether men or women, and bring them to Jerusalem.
precepts.point: Before the followers of Christ were called Christians in Antioch, they were called "this way."

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
Before the followers of Christ were called Christians in Antioch, they were called “this way.”

Saul “desired of him letters to Damascus to the synagogues, that if he found any of this way, whether they were men or women, he might bring them bound unto Jerusalem.” He sought them in the synagogues, men and women, because they were Israelites who followed Christ. They were the way before they were Christians.

precepts.text: Paul confesses he persecuted "this way" unto the death, binding men and women into prisons.
precepts.point: Before the followers of Christ were called Christians in Antioch, they were called "this way."

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
Paul confessed it: “And I persecuted this way unto the death, binding and delivering into prisons both men and women.”

The same Saul who persecuted this way was the one Barnabas went to Tarsus to seek and brought to Antioch, where “a whole year they assembled themselves with the church, and taught much people.” And there the way was first called Christians.

precepts.text: Jesus says, "I am the way, the truth, and the life," which is why the followers were called this way.
precepts.point: Before the followers of Christ were called Christians in Antioch, they were called "this way."

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
“Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.”

That is why the followers were called this way. Christ is the way, so those who followed him were the way, before they were called Christians first in Antioch.

precepts.point: The circumcision was the southern kingdom of Judah, Benjamin, and Levi. The uncircumcised were primarily the northern kingdom.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
The gospel of the uncircumcision was committed to Paul as the gospel of the circumcision was to Peter, both wrought by Christ. The uncircumcision was also called the Gentiles; these terms mean one and the same. “And the apostles and brethren that were in Judea heard that the Gentiles had also received the word of God.” That refers specifically to Cornelius.

“And when Peter was come up to Jerusalem, they that were of the circumcision contended with him, Saying, Thou wentest in to men uncircumcised, and didst eat with them.” The circumcision contended with Peter for going to men uncircumcised: the two groups, circumcision and uncircumcision, are the two ministries of Galatians 2.

points: The apostles and brethren in Judea heard that the Gentiles had also received the word of God, and now Peter is rehearsing what happened in Acts 10. The "Gentiles" is a reference to Cornelius, who was not Italian by nation; he was an Israelite who served as a general over a hundred men in the Roman army, just as today there are black generals and black soldiers in the American army, and America is an extension of ancient Rome.

Peter says "of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons," but that does not mean the Most High has no respect for his chosen nation. He is a respecter of persons concerning his chosen race, and what Peter means is that God shows no partiality in judgment, whether a man is poor or mighty.

"But in every nation he that feareth him and worketh righteousness is accepted with him." The "every nation" is not the Chinese, Japanese, East Indian, or Caucasian; it is every nation into which the Israelites were scattered for disobedience.
To fear him and work righteousness means to keep the commandments; "devout" means to keep the law of the Most High.

Cornelius specifically was of the northern kingdom of Israel; the word was sent unto the children of Israel, and Cornelius was a just man giving alms and keeping the commandments even while scattered.

When Israel was scattered they mingled among the heathen and became Gentiles themselves, taking on the nations' names, customs, idols, and nationalities, just as black Americans today assimilate, calling themselves African-American, Haitian-American, or Latin American, pledging the flag, and eating swine flesh. points: Some of them, men of Cyprus and Cyrene, came to Antioch and spake to the Grecians, preaching the Lord Jesus. Those Grecians, or Hellenists, were Greek-speaking Jews. The Holman Christian Standard Bible calls them Hellenists, and the Zondervan compact Bible dictionary defines a Hellenist as a Jew who made Greek his tongue and adopted Greek ideas and practices.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

points: The hand of the Lord was with them and a great number believed and turned to the Lord. The church at Jerusalem sent Barnabas, a good man full of the Holy Ghost and faith, who exhorted them to cleave to the Lord, then went to Tarsus to seek Saul and brought him to Antioch, where for a whole year they taught much people.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

points: The disciples were called Christians first in Antioch, and those disciples were Jews. Christians were not all nations or races as men think today; the Greek word Christianos comes from Christos, the anointed one, so a Christian is a kinsman of the Messiah and a follower of Christ, an anointed one.
Before the followers of Christ were called Christians in Antioch, they were called "this way."

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

points: In those days prophets came from Jerusalem to Antioch, and one named Agabus signified by the Spirit that there would be a great dearth throughout all the world, which came to pass in the days of Claudius Caesar. This famine is historically documented; Elliott's commentary notes the frequent famines of Claudius's reign, and Josephus records a famine affecting Judea and Syria under the procurator Cuspius Fadus around AD 45, when Queen Helena of Adiabene sent supplies of corn and figs, again giving validity to the Bible as an accurate history book.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

points: The disciples, every man according to his ability, determined to send relief to the brethren in Judea, which they did, sending it to the elders by the hand of Barnabas and Saul. That is the end of Acts 11.
